Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked great and the team is excited about moving from our current pilot to a production integration. Before we lock in the architecture, procurement needs a clear hosted API rate card and an idea of discounts for committed volume. A couple of specifics we care about:

- Sustained monthly commit vs. burstable throughput: we need to understand sustained tokens/month pricing and any burst windows for short spikes.
- Overages: how are overages billed if we exceed the commit in a given month?
- Commitment term tradeoffs: 3-month pilot vs. 12-month commit (what discount bands apply).
- Any minimums or onboarding credits you can extend for a first paid pilot.

I've attached a sanitized usage profile for May so you can see our traffic shape (streamline_usage_profile_May2026.csv). Can you send a one-page rate card (hosted API) and a couple pricing scenarios for 50M, 200M, and 1B tokens/mo? We want something procurement can model quickly.

Hi all — attaching a compact spreadsheet (proposed-pricing-20260519.xlsx) with the bands and some worked examples. Summary below so procurement can model quickly:

Baseline hosted list price (no commit): $2.50 per 1M tokens.
Discount bands off baseline for committed monthly tokens (applies to tokens consumed during month):
- Tier A (50M/mo commit): 10% discount => $2.25 per 1M tokens
- Tier B (200M/mo commit): 18% discount => $2.05 per 1M tokens
- Tier C (1B/mo commit): 30% discount => $1.75 per 1M tokens

Overage handling: any consumption above the committed amount in a given month is billed at the baseline list price (no discount) unless you opt for a blended overage rate in the contract. We can propose a blended overage at an additional 3% over the applied discount in Tier B/C if you need predictable cost on spikes.

Burst allowance and smoothing: for hosted, we commonly include a 15-minute burst window at up to 3x sustained rate to handle traffic spikes; sustained throughput is measured as the 95th percentile of per-minute token rate across the month for gating burst allowances. If you need stricter guaranteed peak SLOs, we recommend Dedicated capacity.

Commit terms:
- Pilot (3 months): no upfront commit, but we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to ~10% of estimated first-month spend) to offset integration/testing costs.
- Standard commit (12 months): applies the discount band for the commit level; early termination has a pro-rated true-up.
- Sustained-commit (24 months): additional 5% on top of the listed discount band for multi-year commitments.

Example scenarios (simplified):
- 50M committed, actual consumption 60M in month => 50M at Tier A rate ($2.25/1M) + 10M overage at baseline ($2.50/1M).
- 200M committed, occasional short spikes to 350M but within burst allowance => billed at Tier B for the month if spikes are within burst.

Notes/assumptions: all pricing is for the hosted API (no Dedicated hardware). We can provide a separate worksheet with blended overage options if Streamline prefers predictable overage rates.

Next: if those bands look reasonable I can convert the spreadsheet to a short commercial summary and proposed MSA terms for a 6-month pilot + 12-month roll option.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference
